scope: Connected residual prctl subsystem: original per-thread comm, parent-death/subreaper controls, SME configuration, original unsupported-command errors, guest copyout/import, proc/diagnostics observations, fork/exec and namespace lifetime.

architecture.dispatch: One residual source/solo ABI. Already migrated credential and seccomp controls retain their original routes. Genuine missing parent/family capabilities defer before effects; missing backend SME support preserves EINVAL.
architecture.name: One original sixteen-byte TaskName, retained by source execution, proc and diagnostics. Only actual name updates/observations take its short object-local mutex, outside guest memory access.
architecture.memory: SET_NAME imports at most fifteen bytes using the original NUL/fault order before committing; GET_NAME validates its full sixteen-byte output. No new guest permission policy, ordinary-memory check/fence, per-instruction hook or global algorithm lock.
architecture.lifetime: Every task clone/fork copies the original comm value, including shared-mm threads. Initial load/exec seed the actual image name and structural publication binds it. Namespace/Files resource replacement preserves the original name identity.
architecture.observations: Proc reads the live original name before cohort drain. Production images no longer store a duplicate command vector; capability-less legacy views retain their old payload. Retained diagnostics read a stack copy of the current original name only when emitting.

validation_notes: All three new process regressions fail against prior production code with only their test-module hook added. Final four/twelve-CPU and one-slot runs retain one cohort and a live proc observation before CPU drain.

The signed four-CPU baseline completes correctly but takes sixteen cohorts, returns prctl twenty-four times and clone twice. Final four/twelve-CPU runs use one cohort with no returned syscall or service. No twelve-CPU before measurement is claimed.

The native fixture uses distinct per-thread input/output and a guest atomic naming barrier: every thread renames before any thread reads its comm. Actual backend SME get/set/inheritance flags are checked.

The dormant fixture setup is a real eight-byte legacy proc read, because its previous unsupported prctl now completes on source. Both prior/final runtimes preserve cold admission coverage and explicitly retain the missing typed payload-provider boundary.

During test construction, the live proc observer initially used a bounded epoch that could drain before a host-control observation; the fixture now uses the existing persistent epoch. Compile-only fixes covered helper visibility/imports, the GuestOutput write callback and a test-only u32 helper. These are not production failures.
The duplicate production proc command-vector payload was removed before final source checks. Unchanged earlier checks were not used as proof for that final source hash.

Final Rust source hashes match Linux CI and the paired Mac checkout. Only documentation/evidence changes follow passing source checks. Mac development gates 1-8 of 12 pass; stable packaging and physical iPad installation are outside this round.
